content:
oliver: Heads-up — I wired a lightweight nightly profiling pipeline that focuses on batching heuristics + KV cache interactions. uploading runs to s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1764008123/ :rocket:

anya: sweet. can you add NVTX ranges around the batch boundary and the KV lookup path? makes kernel grouping in the timeline way easier. :+1:

oliver: yes — I added NVTX markers in runtime v2.3. snippet i used:```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("batch_start");
process_batch(...);
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```

sasha: what flags are you running nsys with? full-system traces blow up storage. we should capture only cuda and osrt + timestamps.

oliver: current command:```
nsys profile --output out --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none \
  --force-overwrite --capture-range=cudaApiTrace --stats=true \n  --capture-forked-processes true -- ./bin/serve-test --profile-tag=1764008123
```

mike: re: storage — we should keep a 30-day rolling window and store summaries forever. big raw traces should be auto-pruned after 7 days unless someone pins them. can the pipeline upload both raw + condensed JSON summary?

ci-runner: perf pipeline: run queued by @oliver at 2025-08-13T03:48:43Z. artifact upload in progress.

perf-bot: automated report: 1 run completed, 3 samples captured. raw artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1764008123/raw/ ; summaries: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1764008123/summary.json

emma: quick perf note — default nsys with full cuda kernel names massively inflates file. try `--trace=cuda,osrt` + `--sample=none` and rely on NVTX to slice. for hotspot detection, we can run short nvprof with `--print-gpu-trace` as second pass.

oliver: agreed. i pushed a change to the harvester to produce a condensed timeline JSON with per-kernel durations and counts. sample excerpt from summary.json:```
"kernels": [
  { "name": "matmul_gemm", "count": "48", "total_ms": "123.4", "pct": "42%" },
  { "name": "softmax", "count": "48", "total_ms": "32.1", "pct": "11%" }
]
```

sasha: that matmul_gemm being 42% pins batching strategy as first suspect. we should compare runs with batch_size=8 vs 16. can pipeline paramize that?

oliver: yes, pipeline job spec supports matrix runs. I launched batch_size=[4,8,16] + kvcache=on/off. will post diffs to the perf-diff dashboard when ready.

mike: add a metadata key for kernel selection policy used (e.g., kernel_selector=v1|v2|heuristic) so diffs are interpretable.

oliver: done. harvester attaches `meta.json` with runtime_git, kernel_selector, env, batch_size.

ci-runner: run finished: 3 variants, total size raw=2.9GB, condensed=1.2MB. upload complete.

perf-bot: diff job scheduled: comparing baseline (1763940000) -> new (1764008123). diff summary will appear at https://perf.redwood.example/diffs/1764008123 in ~10m.

anya: FYI some of the condensed timelines currently drop kernel launch latency edges. we should include host->device enqueue time in the summary so we can spot launch stalls.

emma: sample reduced nsys command i recommend:```
nsys profile -o out --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none \
  --capture-range=cudaApiTrace --stats=true --quiet \
  --force-overwrite -- ./bin/serve-test --batch_size=8 --kvcache=1
```

oliver: noted — i'll add enqueue latency to the summary exporter. also increasing the per-run timeout so we don't miss slow tail kernels.

mike: once diff link is up i'll cherry-pick a few traces for deeper nvprof/nvlink view.

perf-bot: diff ready: https://perf.redwood.example/diffs/1764008123 — regression detected in matmul_gemm (median +18%), possible kernel selection fallback to fp32 path. tagging @sasha @emma @oliver

sasha: ouch. that suggests selector chose a safe kernel variant. we should check kernel_selector logs in meta.json for flags that force fp32.

oliver: pulling logs now. meta shows kernel_selector=heuristic-v3, fallback=fp32_matmul when workspace free_mem<2GB. looks like our batch matrix + kvcache memory pressure triggered fallback.

anya: we should log kvcache hit rate in the summary too — high miss rate can increase effective sequence length and blow memory.

oliver: added kvcache_hit/miss counters to exporter for next runs. will re-run a narrow matrix with forced kernel_selector=v2 to validate.

mike: perfect. also add a note in the perf playbook about preferred nsys flags and pruning rules so infra doesn't have to dig every time.

oliver: will PR the playbook and ping here. thanks everyone. :smile:
